ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 3 — Annual Wellness Visit, Subsequent — Ella Fitzgerald

text.paragraph: Ms. Fitzgerald is a 70-year-old singer with type 2 diabetes and peripheral artery disease, macular edema in the right eye, and coronary bypass surgery last year, who comes for her subsequent annual wellness visit five weeks after her first visit and three weeks after her vascular surgery consultation. Since glipizide was stopped and glargine was moved to the morning, her continuous glucose monitor has shown one reading of 66 mg/dL, on a travel day when lunch was late, and none below 54. She started low-dose rivaroxaban with her aspirin after the consultation and has had no bleeding. She has had two weeks of the supervised walking program and can already walk a little farther. She had her first injection in the right eye two weeks ago and saw the podiatrist last week, who pared the calluses and measured her for low-heeled stage shoes. She has a two-week run of concerts starting next month. [S]

text.paragraph: Vital signs recorded on 2026-06-15; see the Vital Signs section. [S]

tr.td: Well and animated; weight 83.4 kg, BMI 30.6; blood pressure 124/68
Lens implants in both eyes; injection site in the right eye healed; no redness
Whispered voice heard in both ears
Regular rhythm; healed sternotomy scar; no murmur; femoral pulses present; right foot pulses absent and left faint, as before
Calluses pared; hammer toes; skin intact; no ulcer; protective sensation intact
Timed Up and Go 11 seconds without an aid
Oriented; recall and reasoning normal; Mini-Cog 5 of 5
No suspicious lesions on the exposed skin

Type 2 diabetes mellitus with peripheral artery disease: cramping in both calves after about one and a half blocks of walking, worse on the right, easing within minutes of rest; no rest pain, wounds, or color change. Resting ankle-brachial index 0.62 right and 0.74 left, toe-brachial index 0.46 and 0.55; dorsalis pedis and posterior tibial pulses absent on the right and faint on the left. A1c 8.6% on metformin, glipizide and glargine, with low glucose readings (to 52 mg/dL) after late performances. Foot: protective sensation intact to the 10-g monofilament at all sites and to vibration; callus under the second metatarsal heads; hammer toes of the second and third toes; no ulcer (IWGDF risk category 2). Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented diabetes and its circulatory complications
S — Synthetic modern diagnosis; the type of diabetes was not made public and is synthetic.

Moderate nonproliferative diabetic retinopathy with center-involving diabetic macular edema in the right eye (best-corrected acuity 64 letters, about 20/50) and moderate nonproliferative retinopathy without macular edema in the left eye (81 letters); lens implants in both eyes from earlier cataract surgery. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented diabetic eye problems
S — Synthetic modern eye diagnosis on retinal imaging and optical coherence tomography in the clinic; the left eye is described in the display.

Coronary artery disease after five-vessel coronary bypass surgery last year, with an intensive care stay; no angina now; on aspirin, a statin, and metoprolol. Synthetic modern episode linked to her documented heart surgery
S — Synthetic modern coding of her documented heart surgery; bypass grafts are described in the display.

Next annual wellness visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 2026-08-10: three-month review: A1c, lipids, walking program, eye treatment, and foot care. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 18 minutes, with her consent. She reviewed the written directive she made before her heart surgery and confirmed a health care agent, recorded in the confidential part of the chart and not named here. She said that what matters most to her is to keep singing and travelling for as long as she can, and to keep her sight. She will review the directive yearly. [S]
